out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Water Temp
violations.observation: Observed hot water at hand sink 77-85F during inspection.
violations.corrective_action: A handwashing sink shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. Please ensure hot water at hand sink is at least 100F.

violations.title: Food Thermometers, Provided & Accessible
violations.observation: The certified food manager could not provide a food temperature measuring device. Observed no food thermometer in facility.
violations.corrective_action: A metal-stemmed probe food thermometer shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures. Please order food thermometer and forward invoice to EHS within 10 days.

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Manual Wash Water Temperature
violations.observation: The temperature of the in-use wash water solution was observed at less than 110F. Observed hot water at 3 compartment sink at 85F.
violations.corrective_action: The temperature of the wash solution for manual warewashing machine must be no less than 110F or the temperature specified on the cleaning agent manufacturer's label instructions. Please ensure hot water at 3 compartment sink at 110F.

out_items.name: Hot and cold water available, adequate pressure

violations.title: Water Capacity to Meet Peak Demands
violations.observation: The water source and system serving this food service establishment has been interrupted. Observed insufficient hot water in facility during inspection. Hot water capacity with current water heater is sufficient.
violations.corrective_action: The water source and system shall be of sufficient capacity to meet the peak water demands of the food establishment. Person in charge contacted maintenance during inspection. Please contact EHS once hot water is sufficient.
